_comment: Tunable knobs for scripts/job-radar.mjs. Edit here, no code changes needed. Titles/experience feed the Apify career-site actor; keywords drive profile scoring.
_timezone_comment: Runs on GitHub Actions (cloud, always-on), which is UTC. This timezone governs the radar's morning-sweep/aggregator-hour logic (hourInTz), independent of the runner's clock and of outreach.google.timezone (Pacific, used by other scripts). Set to Eastern so the schedule tracks the earliest US (East Coast) posting hours. The cron in .github/workflows/job-radar.yml fires hourly 5am-10pm ET.
_range_comment: career-site actor (fantastic-jobs) ONLY accepts timeRange values 1h/24h/7d/6m. It is pay-per-JOB ($0.012/job), so cost tracks jobs fetched, not run count -> hourly + 1h window fetches each job once (cost-optimal). Do NOT use 2h/12h (invalid -> Apify 400, silently zeroes out career). The 5am ET run uses 24h (capped by limitMorningSweep) to sweep up anything posted during the overnight gap (10pm-5am ET) so early East Coast openings are never missed; the seen-store dedups so overlap is never re-notified.
_sources_comment: career-site runs every scheduled hour (cheap, 1h window). The 5am ET run uses morningSweepRange (24h, capped) as the overnight/East-Coast catch-up. The aggregator boards (linkedin, handshake) are pay-per-result, so they run once/day on sweepHours (8am ET). Toggle any board with sources.<id>.enabled.

linkedin._note: Dedicated LinkedIn jobs actor (sourabhbgp/linkedin-jobs-scraper) at $0.0005/result. Replaces JobSpy's LinkedIn module, which returned zero LinkedIn rows. LinkedIn's AI search ignores experienceLevel, so we run one 'any' pass per term and rely on the post-fetch title-exclusion + experienceYearsCap filters. enrichDetails=true gives full descriptions.

indeed._note: DISABLED 2026-08-26 (budget): misceres/indeed-scraper at $0.005/job x 150/day = ~$22/mo — the 2nd-biggest cost and ~90% redundant with career-site (Indeed mostly re-lists the same ATS jobs). Re-enable if career-site coverage proves thin.

jobspy._note: DISABLED 2026-08-26: slow + repeatedly aborted at our 420s guard (wasting compute), and its LinkedIn module was dead. Indeed coverage moved to misceres/indeed-scraper; Google Jobs dropped as redundant (it re-lists Indeed/LinkedIn we already fetch).

wellfound._note: DISABLED 2026-08-21: many returned listing URLs were dead/expired, and it was the 2nd-most-expensive board ($2.41 in testing). Re-enable only if URL quality improves.

dice._note: DISABLED 2026-08-26 (budget): ~$3/mo but returns mostly senior/agency W2 contract listings (Apex Lead, Rapsys 12-mo contract) that get dropped by the experience/title filters anyway. Low signal-to-cost. Re-enable if needed.

jobright._note: DISABLED: the only available actor (jobscrawler/jobright-scraper) returns placeholder/mock rows (verified 2026-08-21 — company 'InnovateTech', templated descriptions). JobRight.ai also re-aggregates the same Greenhouse/Lever/LinkedIn inventory the other sources already cover. Re-enable if a reliable actor appears.

query._titleSearch_comment: Trimmed 2026-08-26 to core high-fit families (22 -> 11) to cut career-site volume/cost. career-site is pay-per-job, so each distinct role family adds ~fetch volume. Removed broader/higher-volume families (DevOps/Cloud/Platform/Applied Scientist/Research Engineer/Applications Developer) to fit budget; SRE kept for the k8s cred. Re-add families here if you want more breadth (raises cost ~proportionally).
query._titleExclusionExtra_comment: Post-fetch-only strict tokens (applied by buildExclusionRe, NOT sent to the career-site actor). Kept separate so single letters/roman numerals don't confuse the actor's title search. 'I' is intentionally NOT here so 'Engineer I' still passes.
query._experienceYearsCap_comment: Breadth C: keep general SWE roles, but drop any that state a hard experience minimum ABOVE this many years (e.g. '5+ years required'). Uses the BINDING (largest) required minimum across all stated requirements, so a Lead role that also lists '1+ years with X' is still dropped. Roles with no stated minimum, or '0-2 years', pass.
query._freshness_comment: Keep the digest fresh. maxPostAgeDays=1 drops any row posted 2+ days ago (only when a real date is present) -> today + yesterday only. Source lookbacks are also tightened to ~1 day (dice=ONE, handshake=today, linkedin=past24h, career=2h/12h) so stale rows are never fetched.
query._reposts_comment: The LinkedIn actor exposes no repost flag, so maxApplicants is used as a proxy: rows with more applicants than this (LinkedIn's 'Over 100 people clicked apply' bucket) are dropped as stale/oversubscribed reposts. Set to null to disable.
query._titleRequireAny_comment: Positive title gate for aggregator boards (LinkedIn/Indeed/Dice fuzzy-match, so a 'software engineer' search also returns Data Science, Analyst, Helpdesk, Land Development, etc.). A normalized title must contain at least one of these software-domain tokens to survive. career-site already gates titles server-side via titleSearch, and every titleSearch phrase contains one of these tokens, so it is unaffected.

scoring._comment: Keyword -> weight. Summed over title + AI skills + description. Higher = better profile fit; digest is sorted by score.
